seo.title: What is a vector embedding?
seo.description: A vector embedding turns a piece of text into a list of numbers that places it near other text with a similar meaning.

definition: A vector embedding turns a piece of text into a list of numbers that places it near other text with a similar meaning.
answerBlock: A vector embedding turns a piece of text into a list of numbers that places it near other text with a similar meaning. It is what lets a search find "how much does a rebuild cost" when the page says "what moves the price". The comparison is of meaning, not of matching words.

body.heading: What are embeddings used for on a website?
paragraphs: Search that understands synonyms, recommendations that are actually related, grouping support enquiries by topic, and the retrieval step that feeds a language model the right passages.

They are generated by a model and stored in a database that can compare them quickly. Practical questions are how often they are regenerated when content changes, and whether the text ever leaves your infrastructure to be embedded.

They are not magic. Embedding search finds things that are similar in meaning, which is not always the same as finding the right answer, so it is usually combined with ordinary keyword search rather than replacing it.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: For a catalogue or a documentation set, meaning-based search converts "I could not find it" into an order or a self-served answer.
The cost is in keeping the index current, which is an operational commitment rather than a one-off build.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: A support search that matches "invoice on account" with pages about purchase orders and payment terms, rather than returning nothing because the exact phrase is not used.

service.title: AI integration
service.line: Qualification assistants, search, content tooling and workflow automation wired into your own data.

terms.definition: A large language model is software trained on very large amounts of text that predicts likely continuations, which is why it can write and summarise.
Retrieval-augmented generation is the pattern of finding the relevant documents first and giving them to a language model with the question.
